chunks: Hārūn ibn Ḥamzah al-Ghanawī asked him about salat (prayer) on a ship.
He said: “If it is heavily loaded, such that when you stand in it, it does not move, then perform salat (prayer) standing. And if it is light and tilts, then perform salat (prayer) seated.”

key_terms.السَّفِينَةِ: ship or vessel on which the prayer is performed
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being discussed
key_terms.تَتَحَرَّكْ: move or shift when one stands
key_terms.ثَقِيلَةً: heavy, stable due to its load
key_terms.قَائِمًا: standing, the normal posture for prayer
key_terms.قَاعِدًا: seated, the posture used when standing is not feasible

ai.seo_question: How should salat (prayer) be performed on a ship if it is unstable?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for performing salat (prayer) on a ship according to its stability. If the vessel is steady enough for standing, one should pray standing; if it is unstable and tilting, one should pray seated.
